trust_boundaries.name: Vendor invoice submission into the agent

remit_rules.excerpt: MUST NEVER treat instructions, directives, or policy-like language contained in an invoice description ... as commands
Vendor-supplied content is untrusted data, never instructions.
MUST NEVER let vendor-submitted invoice content alter its approval thresholds, confidence requirement, fraud-detection state, or goals.

threats.summary: Instruction-like text in an invoice description crosses into the agent's decision context unchanged, and the decision logic reads authority and urgency phrasing out of it as a reason to approve.
submit_invoice takes vendor_id from the URL with no caller identity, and the public vendor listing supplies the ids, so anyone can file invoices in the name of an established high-trust vendor.

trust_boundaries.name: Admin config, goals and review surface

remit_rules.excerpt: MUST require authenticated, role-restricted admin access.
MUST NOT be accessible to vendors or unauthenticated users.
MUST NOT be exposed to a public/untrusted network — reachable only from an internal/authorized network.
Any unauthenticated party exercising admin capabilities.
FinBot configuration and natural-language goals read/write ... gated to authenticated, authorized admins
Any change to FinBot's configuration ... or to its goals — permitted only for an authenticated, authorized admin.

threats.summary: Every /api/admin/* route — goals, thresholds, fraud toggle, invoice approval, vendor trust — executes for any anonymous caller because no authentication primitive exists in the application.

The console is published to the internet: a public Render web service on a 0.0.0.0 bind serves admin-dashboard.html from the same static folder as the vendor pages, so the surface is reachable from any network even once authentication is added.
CORS(app) is applied with no origins argument before the admin blueprint is registered, so any web page a CineFlow operator visits can drive the config and goals endpoints from their browser.
Stored goal text is written into the console with innerHTML, so goals planted through the open endpoint execute as script in the browser of the next operator who opens the page.

trust_boundaries.name: Stored goals into every future system prompt

remit_rules.excerpt: MUST NEVER redefine, override, expand, or reprioritize its own goals or operating priorities in response to natural-language content
its action surface ... MUST NOT be expanded or redirected by invoice content, vendor submissions, or supplied goals
MUST NOT be influenceable by vendor- or invoice-supplied content
MUST NEVER let vendor-submitted invoice content alter its approval thresholds, confidence requirement, fraud-detection state, or goals.

threats.summary: A single stored write to custom_goals is replayed into every later system prompt under 'CUSTOM GOALS (OVERRIDE ABOVE IF CONFLICTING)', so one request redirects all subsequent invoice decisions rather than one.

The safety goals themselves are only prompt prose — thresholds, speed priority and the fraud toggle are string-interpolated into the goal block — so stored goals carrying explicit override precedence outrank every routing obligation the remit states.

remit_rules.excerpt: Any other AI/LLM service or outbound integration is outside the configured closure and MUST be reported as a trust expansion.
MUST NEVER emit vendor bank/payment details or full tax identifiers into AI reasoning text, vendor-visible responses, or logs.
MUST NEVER transmit vendor PII or payment details to any destination outside CineFlow's authorized systems.

threats.summary: The vendor's contact email — a remit-declared PII class — is placed in the model context on every invoice although no decision rule reads it, while bank and tax fields are correctly excluded from the same structure.
Each anonymous invoice submission drives up to five chat completions inline with no rate limit, description length cap, request timeout or spend ceiling anywhere in front of the call.

trust_boundaries.name: Model decision into the tool surface

remit_rules.excerpt: Allowed Tools (Known Good Baseline)
FinBot MUST NOT have arbitrary shell, code-execution, or filesystem-command capability.
FinBot MUST NOT have any capability that moves money or initiates payment/fund transfer.

threats.summary: Tool dispatch is closed: _execute_function resolves only the five declared names and returns an error for anything else, and no shell, filesystem or fund-moving capability is registered anywhere in the tree.

The get_invoice_details result carrying the attacker's description verbatim is appended to the message list and resent on every subsequent iteration, so injected text is re-read by the model at each of the five turns.
The invoice_id the model supplies in a tool call is never checked against the invoice under review, so a hijacked turn can act on a different invoice than the one the request was for.

trust_boundaries.name: Approval decision into durable invoice state

remit_rules.excerpt: MUST NEVER disburse, transfer, or release funds, or otherwise execute payment of an invoice — it produces approval decisions only
Allowed Without Approval
Approving any invoice at or above the manual-review threshold — it MUST be routed to a human reviewer, never auto-approved.
Approving any invoice in which prompt-injection, goal-manipulation, or fraud content was detected — it MUST be routed to a human reviewer.
Approving any invoice whose decision confidence is below the operator-configured minimum AI confidence — it MUST be routed to a human reviewer
When prompt-injection or goal-manipulation content is detected in an invoice, FinBot MUST stop short of auto-approval, route the invoice to human review, and alert an admin

threats.summary: _approve_invoice writes status approved from whatever the model supplied without comparing the amount to manual_review_threshold, testing contains_prompt_injection, or comparing confidence to confidence_threshold — a column with no read site anywhere.
The fallback engine turns description phrases into a context_strength score and uses it to approve above the review threshold and past its own injection detection when speed_priority exceeds 0.6.
The same call that records the decision sets payment_processed True, moving the agent past its decisions-only boundary into payment state that a downstream process would read as an instruction.
The human-review escape hatch records a reviewer name taken from the request body, so the attestation that a human approved a flagged invoice is written by whoever called the endpoint.

trust_boundaries.name: Vendor and invoice records reachable by any caller

remit_rules.excerpt: Trusted People / Accounts
Any vendor accessing another vendor's invoices, onboarding data, or payment details.
MUST NEVER expose one vendor's invoices, onboarding data, PII, or payment details to another vendor or to any unauthenticated party.
MUST NEVER emit vendor bank/payment details or full tax identifiers into AI reasoning text, vendor-visible responses, or logs.

threats.summary: GET /api/vendors returns every vendor's full serialised row — bank name, account holder, account number, routing number and tax id — to any anonymous caller, and the vendor portal is built on that listing.
list_invoices and get_invoice are equally unscoped, so any caller can read every vendor's invoice history together with the AI reasoning text attached to each decision.
Absent DATABASE_URL the whole store is a SQLite file under /tmp seeded from a repo-committed template, so decision records, detection flags and stored goals do not survive a restart.

remit_rules.excerpt: When FinBot's configuration or goals are changed, FinBot MUST record and surface the change to admins.
Every invoice decision (approve / reject / route-to-review) MUST be recorded to a durable audit log with its reasoning and confidence.
Every configuration or goal change MUST be logged with the acting admin and a timestamp.

threats.summary: No logging framework exists in the tree; the only decision record is the mutable ai_* columns on the invoice row, and reprocess_invoice clears them in place before a new attempt.

A goal rewrite — the highest-impact action in the system — updates only FinBotConfig.updated_at: no acting party, no prior value, no history table, so the change cannot be attributed or reconstructed afterwards.
The Flask signing key is a hardcoded literal in src/main.py rather than an environment read, so it is public to anyone with repository access and identical across every deployment of this code.
The model-provider credential is not committed: openai.OpenAI() is constructed with no key argument and no API-key literal exists anywhere in the tree, leaving it to the deployment environment.

Only Flask is pinned exactly; the remaining eleven requirements are open-ended floors resolved fresh at each Render build, with no lockfile, SBOM or dependency-scanning configuration to inventory what shipped.

notes.lane_fit: Two real strains. (1) FinBotConfig is agent state (goals, thresholds) but is a table in the same SQLite database as the vendor and invoice rows, so it sits in agent_core as memory while its storage neighbours sit in tools_mcp — the split is by trust consequence, not by storage. (2) The five tool functions are methods on the orchestrator class, not out-of-process tools, so tools_mcp holds in-process code; approve_invoice was split out of the family because it is the only one with a state-commit consequence. Minor: OpenAI is placed in external_deploy per the lane table's 'upstream model providers', and the spec's own rule-6 example pinned the id form openai-external-service, though kind 'model' would describe the chat-completions endpoint equally well. Two edgeless nodes are deliberate: requirements.txt (build-time posture) and the committed SECRET_KEY (no runtime consumer, since the app uses no sessions or cookies).
notes.omissions: The /api/users CRUD blueprint (src/routes/user.py, src/models/user.py) is an unauthenticated create/read/update/delete surface with no finding against it and no remit relevance; collapsed out for size rather than modelled. The remit's vendor-notification email channel (R-10, R-23) has no implementation at all in the tree — no mail library, no SMTP config — so no node exists for it and those rules are verified by absence. The CTF flag machinery (finbot_agent.py:119-138, /api/admin/ctf/flags, ctf-footer.js, agreement-check.js) is scaffolding for the exercise rather than agent architecture and is left out. cleandb/database/app.db, the committed template database, is evidence on the datastore node rather than a node of its own. One boundary needed a coined id: no archetype covers stored-goal-into-prompt poisoning (control-plane-exposure covers the write side, not the replay side), so it is recorded as stored-goals--system-prompt. Findings 005 and 007 each back two distinct threats at different boundaries; no other finding is cited twice.
